claims.claim: Amphilochius of Iconium was a fourth‑century Christian bishop who served as bishop of Iconium (modern Konya, Turkey) from about 374 until his death around 394‑403.

He was born around 339‑340 in Caesarea in Cappadocia, came from a distinguished Cappadocian family, studied law under the rhetorician Libanius, practiced as a lawyer in Constantinople, and retired to a religious life before his episcopal consecration.
Amphilochius was a close associate of the Cappadocian Fathers—Basil of Caesarea and Gregory of Nazianzus—and he attended the First Council of Constantinople in 381.
The work “On Holy Saturday (In diem sabbati sancti)” is a homily that Amphilochius composed for the liturgical celebration of Holy Saturday, the day that commemorates the burial of Christ.
The homily was delivered to the faithful of his diocese on the Great and Holy Saturday of the Paschal week, addressing the congregation gathered for the burial feast of the Savior.
In the sermon Amphilochius emphasizes Christ’s victory over death and Hades and includes a polemical section against the Jews, portraying their attempts to guard the tomb as futile.
The sermon reflects the early church’s theological motif that Holy Saturday celebrates Christ’s conquest of death and the liberation of the dead.
